content:
The Shiu family returned home this afternoon to sort through family photographs, ancestral coins, calligraphy and paintings, as well as some clothing. However, due to time constraints and the fact that the unit has had its water and electricity disconnected, they were unable to organize all their belongings and plan to return next week to continue tidying up. In the past, the Shiu family had installed CCTV outside the house. After the land resumption operation, when they returned home, they found that the relevant CCTV had been covered with plastic bags.

The Lands Department recently replied twice that it was only when the department arranged to hand over the structures to the Civil Engineering and Development Department earlier this year that Mr. Shiu suddenly moved into the squatter hut, and that he was a public housing tenant who did not meet the resettlement eligibility. It also stressed that the Lands Department, together with the social work team, had been in contact with Mr. Shiu since the beginning of the year.

The Shiu family earlier told *集誌社* that after the father-in-law passed away in 2019, her husband and other siblings jointly inherited the land title through estate administration, and signed off on the land compensation two years ago, but they still have not received the compensation payment. The Shiu family continued to rebut this today, saying that during the 2016 Cha Kwo Ling village fire, her husband was already at the scene, escaping with his mother and five pets, and the media even conducted interviews and filming at the time. They are dissatisfied with the Lands Department's claim that her husband was a mid-term entrant.

Another allegation from the Shiu family is that they have not received compensation since signing the land compensation documents. The Lands Department earlier confirmed that part of the land concerned is government land and part is private land. The former owner of the private land has accepted the government's land compensation offer, but the relevant documents are still awaiting signature by the former owner's representative lawyer. The Lands Department said that upon receiving the signed documents, it will disburse the land compensation as soon as possible.
